paragraphs.text: וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הוּרַ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מִיַּד֙ הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef was brought down to Mitsrayim; and Potifar, an officer of Pharaoh's, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Yishme'elim, who had brought him down thither.

paragraphs.commentary: Potifar's two court-titles, *seris Par'oh* and *sar ha-tabbachim*, repeat from Gen 37:36, where Yosef was first sold to him. *Saris* (H5631, the Akkadian loanword *ša rēši*) is ambiguous between the functional 'court-official / officer' and the literal 'eunuch'; the ASV-baseline **'officer'** is retained, with the eunuch-sense and its tension against the married Potifar of this very chapter (the *eshet adonav* of v 7) documented at the central entry *saris-court-official-eunuch-ambiguity*. *Sar ha-tabbachim* is literally 'chief of the slaughterers'; ASV-baseline **'captain of the guard'** is retained, with the 'chief steward' (NJPS) and 'chief executioner' alternatives at *sar-ha-tabbachim-captain-of-the-guard*. Both central entries' *appliesTo* are extended here to add GEN-WOH-39:1 — a scope-formalization of titles already governed (their rationales named Gen 39-41 as extensible), not a new lexical decision.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְהִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ וַיְהִ֕י בְּבֵ֖ית אֲדֹנָ֥יו הַמִּצְרִֽי׃

i18n.en: And YHWH was with Yosef, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's refrain begins here: *va-yehi YHWH et-Yosef* — 'and YHWH was with Yosef.' The divine name is the Tetragrammaton **YHWH**, rendered per the confirmed corpus convention (re-verified at Gen 38:7, 10; 'Yahweh' deferred to a future corpus-wide retransliteration pass). What is distinctive: Genesis 39 is the ONLY chapter in the Yosef cycle (Gen 37-50) in which the narrator's divine name is YHWH rather than Elohim — the name recurs as the chapter's structural frame at vv 3, 5, 21, 23. This divine-name distribution is one of the classic source-critical data of the Yosef novella, commonly read as a Yahwistic (J) frame around an otherwise Elohistic composition (Wellhausen; Driver; von Rad; Westermann; Coats; Redford; Friedman). See v 9 for the contrasting Elohim on Yosef's own lips; the full observation is documented at the overlay entry *yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim*. No WoH synthesis about the divine names is imported; the source-critical reading is recorded as named mainstream scholarship only.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲדֹנָ֔יו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And his master saw that YHWH was with him, and that YHWH made all that he did to prosper in his hand.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּפְקִדֵ֙הוּ֙ עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְכָל־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yosef found favor in his sight, and he ministered unto him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֞י בִּרְכַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ בַּבַּ֖יִת וּבַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass from the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that YHWH blessed the Egyptian's house for Yosef's sake; and the blessing of YHWH was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֮ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵף֒ וְלֹא־יָדַ֤ע אִתּוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אוֹכֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף יְפֵה־תֹ֖אַר וִיפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And he left all that he had in Yosef's hand; and he knew not aught that was with him, save the bread which he did eat. And Yosef was beautiful in form, and fair to look upon.

paragraphs.commentary: The closing epithet *yefeh-to'ar vifeh mar'eh* — 'beautiful in form, and fair to look upon' — is rendered ASV-baseline and, deliberately, **identically to Gen 29:17**, where the same double-formula describes **Rachel**, Yosef's mother (there *yefat-to'ar vifat mar'eh*, with feminine endings). These are the only two people in Genesis given this exact formula. The verbatim repetition is a recognized narrative link: Yosef inherits his mother's beauty, and — since the double-epithet is elsewhere a *woman's* beauty-formula — its application to Yosef structurally casts him as the *object* of another's desire, motivating the seduction-plot it immediately precedes (*va-tissa eshet-adonav et-eineha el-Yosef*, v 7). See Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 272; Alter *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 223 (the gender-reversal); documented at the overlay entry *yefeh-toar-beauty-formula-rachel-yosef*.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַתִּשָּׂ֧א אֵֽשֶׁת־אֲדֹנָ֛יו אֶת־עֵינֶ֖יהָ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁכְבָ֥ה עִמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Yosef; and she said, Lie with me.

paragraphs.text: וַיְמָאֵ֓ן ׀ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣שֶׁת אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יָדַ֥ע אִתִּ֖י מַה־בַּבָּ֑יִת וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדִֽי׃

i18n.en: But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master knoweth not what is with me in the house, and he hath put all that he hath into my hand.

paragraphs.text: אֵינֶ֨נּוּ גָד֜וֹל בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּה֮ מִמֶּנִּי֒ וְלֹֽא־חָשַׂ֤ךְ מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־אוֹתָ֖ךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨יךְ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֜ה הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְחָטָ֖אתִי לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: He is not greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back anything from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim?

paragraphs.commentary: At the climax of Yosef's refusal the divine name switches: *ve-chatati le-Elohim* — 'and sin against **Elohim**.' Against the chapter's YHWH-frame (the narrator's name at vv 2, 3, 5, 21, 23), Elohim is the name on the character's own lips. The narrator-YHWH / character-Elohim split is read either as the J-narrator framing a scene in which an Israelite within an Egyptian household naturally uses the more general *Elohim*, or as a seam where Yahwistic framing brackets an older novella-core. The divine names are rendered exactly as the source distributes them and are not harmonized; see v 2 and the overlay entry *yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim*.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י כְּדַבְּרָ֥הּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף י֣וֹם ׀ י֑וֹם וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as she spake to Yosef day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א הַבַּ֖יְתָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת מְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass about this time, that he went into the house to do his work; and there was none of the men of the house there within.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂ֧הוּ בְּבִגְד֛וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר שִׁכְבָ֣ה עִמִּ֑י וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

i18n.en: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔הּ כִּֽי־עָזַ֥ב בִּגְד֖וֹ בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֖נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ בָּ֤א אֵלַי֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמִּ֔י וָאֶקְרָ֖א בְּק֥וֹל גָּדֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: that she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in a Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:

paragraphs.commentary: Two terms carry weight in the accusation. *Ish Ivri* ('a Hebrew') is the first time Yosef is called *ha-Ivri* in the narrative; the gentilic functions across the patriarchal corpus as an *outsider's* designation, used by foreigners of Israelites or by Israelites to foreigners (cf. *Avram ha-Ivri*, Gen 14:13; Yosef again at 40:15, 41:12; the food-segregation at 43:32). Potifar's wife foregrounds it as a term of ethnic contempt — the household shamed by a *foreigner*. ASV-baseline 'a Hebrew'; see the central entry *ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology* (whose Gen 39 *appliesTo* refs are normalized here to the corpus GEN-WOH- form). The verb *le-tzachek banu* ('to mock us') is the Piel infinitive of *tz-ch-q* — the laughter-root underlying the name *Yitzchaq* — turned here to its darkest register: a false accusation of sexual outrage, with the hostile/sexual-mockery sense (NJPS 'to dally with us'; the accusation continues 'he came in unto me to lie with me'). ASV-baseline 'to mock us' is retained, keeping the hostility without committing the surface to the explicit sexual rendering; the sense and the *Yitzchaq* wordplay are documented at the overlay entry *le-tzachek-mockery-piel-gen39*, the Gen 39 sibling of the central tz-ch-q entries at Gen 21:9 and 26:8.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְשָׁמְע֔וֹ כִּֽי־הֲרִימֹ֥תִי קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ אֶצְלִ֔י וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

i18n.en: and it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled, and got him out.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּנַּ֥ח בִּגְד֖וֹ אֶצְלָ֑הּ עַד־בּ֥וֹא אֲדֹנָ֖יו אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And she laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

paragraphs.text: וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּֽא־אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, whom thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:

paragraphs.commentary: The wife repeats the accusation to Potifar, now sharpening *ish Ivri* (v 14) to *ha-eved ha-Ivri* — 'the Hebrew servant' — pressing both the foreigner-status and the slave-status. The Piel *le-tzachek bi* ('to mock me') is the same verb as v 14 in the same hostile/sexual register. ASV-baseline retained; see the entries *ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology* and *le-tzachek-mockery-piel-gen39*, governing vv 14 and 17 together.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּהֲרִימִ֥י קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֥ב בִּגְד֛וֹ אֶצְלִ֖י וַיָּ֥נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃

i18n.en: and it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled out.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עָ֥שָׂהּ לִ֖י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אסורי [אֲסִירֵ֥י] הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲסוּרִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

i18n.en: And Yosef's master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef is confined in the *beit ha-sohar* — 'the house of the *sohar*' — the chapter's standing word for his prison (vv 20-23) and the setting of the Gen 40-41 dream-interpretation sequence. *Sohar* (H5470) is a rare noun confined to the Yosef cycle; its etymology is debated (a 'round / enclosure' structure; possibly an Egyptian loanword for a fortress-prison; or a by-form of a confinement-noun), all converging on a secured detention-structure distinct from the improvised dry *bor* ('pit / cistern') of Gen 37. ASV-baseline **'prison'** is retained — the functional sense is uncontested and the etymology too uncertain to license a marked surface rendering; documented at the central entry *beit-ha-sohar-prison-round-house*. **Ketiv/qere:** the relative clause has ketiv אסורי (*asurei*, defective, without yod) and qere אֲסִירֵי (*asirei*, plene); the **qere** *asirei* ('the king's prisoners') is translated, per the rule to render the qere. The variation is a defective-vs-plene spelling of the same construct noun with no semantic divergence; no glossary entry warranted.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֵּ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו חָ֑סֶד וַיִּתֵּ֣ן חִנּ֔וֹ בְּעֵינֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר בֵּית־הַסֹּֽהַר׃

i18n.en: But YHWH was with Yosef, and showed kindness unto him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

paragraphs.commentary: The prison-turn is told in covenant-loyalty language: the chapter's *va-yehi YHWH et-Yosef* refrain (v 2) returns, now glossed *va-yet elav chased* — 'and inclined *chesed* toward him.' This is **solitary *chesed*** (H2617), the central Hebrew Bible relational-virtue noun (loyal-love, steadfast-love, covenant-loyalty — Glueck; Sakenfeld's reading of the stronger party's unforced act toward the weaker fits Yosef-in-prison precisely). It is distinct from the word-pair *chesed v-emet*: the surface keeps the ASV-baseline **'showed kindness unto him'**, and the covenant-loyalty range and the *natah... chesed* 'inclining' idiom are documented at the new central entry *chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness* (the companion to, not a duplicate of, the *chesed-v-emet* pair-entry; solitary *chesed* is rendered, not preserved untranslated). The *sar beit ha-sohar* ('keeper of the prison') is governed by *beit-ha-sohar-prison-round-house*.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֙הַר֙ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣אֲסִירִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ שָׁ֔ם ה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

i18n.en: And the keeper of the prison committed to Yosef's hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֣ין ׀ שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־כָּל־מְא֙וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה מַצְלִֽיחַ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: The keeper of the prison looked not to anything that was under his hand, because YHWH was with him; and that which he did, YHWH made it to prosper.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter closes by reprising its opening frame (cf. vv 2-3): *YHWH ito* ('YHWH was with him') and *YHWH matzliach* ('YHWH made it to prosper') — the prison-keeper's delegation to Yosef mirrors Potifar's delegation in vv 4-6, binding the house-section and the prison-section into a single YHWH-with-Yosef structure. The closing YHWH (the eighth and ninth occurrences in the chapter) completes the chapter-distinctive YHWH-frame noted at v 2.
